outlooks.summary: A LINE OF STORMS...POTENTIALLY PRODUCING MAINLY DAMAGING WINDS...SHOULD BE ONGOING THIS MORNING ACROSS EXTREME NORTHWEST TO NORTH-CENTRAL MINNESOTA. ADDITIONAL SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP LATE THIS AFTERNOON ALONG A COLD FRONT AS IT MOVES THROUGH MINNESOTA...EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...AND NORTHWEST IOWA...REACHING NORTHWEST WISCONSIN AND WESTERN UPPER MICHIGAN THIS EVENING. A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS NEBRASKA TO NORTHEAST COLORADO LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MODELS CONTINUE TO INDICATE BROAD/FLAT RIDGING ALOFT PREVAILING ACROSS MOST OF THE U.S. TODAY...WITH LOWS/TROUGHS LINGERING OVER THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST AND OFF THE EAST COAST. FAST WESTERLY FLOW AT MID-UPPER LEVELS WILL BE CONFINED TO THE NORTHERN U.S. AND ADJACENT SOUTHERN CANADA. A FAST-MOVING SHORT-WAVE TROUGH REMAINS FORECAST TO SKIRT THE U.S./CANADA BORDER REGION /FROM MT EARLY TO NORTHERN ONTARIO BY TONIGHT/...WHILE ANOTHER TROUGH AMPLIFIES SOUTHEAST ACROSS CENTRAL CANADA TO THE NORTHERN EXTENT OF THE UPPER MIDWEST BY 12Z MONDAY. AT THE SURFACE...AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE WILL MOVE TO THE NORTHEAST FROM CENTRAL ND INTO CANADA THIS MORNING...WITH A TRAILING COLD FRONT ADVANCING EAST FROM THE DAKOTAS TO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION THIS FORECAST PERIOD. THE WESTERN PORTION OF THIS FRONT SHOULD MOVE MORE SLOWLY SOUTHWARD ACROSS NEB TODAY AND TONIGHT.

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST TO WESTERN UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: STRONG SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL WINDS /UP TO 50-55 KT/ WILL SPREAD ACROSS FAR NORTHERN MN INTO THE ADJACENT WESTERN PORTION OF NORTHERN ONTARIO THIS MORNING. THE SOUTHERN EXTENT OF AN ONGOING MCS...WITH THE POTENTIAL TO BE PRODUCING SEVERE WIND GUSTS...IS EXPECTED TO BE MOVING INTO NORTHWEST MN AT 12Z TODAY. THIS STORM COMPLEX SHOULD CONTINUE TO POSE SOME SEVERE-WEATHER THREAT...AT LEAST...AS IT SPREADS INTO NORTH-CENTRAL MN THIS MORNING...WITH A MAJORITY OF THE MCS AFFECTING NORTHERN ONTARIO. MEANWHILE...STRONG SURFACE HEATING ACROSS NORTHERN MN IN THE WAKE OF THE MORNING STORMS AND SOUTHWARD ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR COMBINED WITH A RELATIVELY NARROW CORRIDOR OF SURFACE DEW POINTS INTO THE UPPER 60S AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL RESULT IN MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE UP TO 2500-3000 J PER KG/. SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL WINDS WILL RESTRENGTHEN BY LATE AFTERNOON AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT...WITH WIND FIELDS ALSO STRENGTHENING ALOFT AND VEERING TO WESTERLY AT 500-MB TO 250-MB. THE DEEP-LAYER WIND PROFILE WILL FAVOR SHEAR VECTORS UP TO 50+ KT AND CROSSING THE COLD FRONT. A CAP IS EXPECTED TO PRECLUDE STORM DEVELOPMENT UNTIL LATE AFTERNOON WITH THE ARRIVAL OF THE COLD FRONT INTO MN AND EAS

sections.title: NEB TO NORTHEAST CO
sections.text: GIVEN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE BROAD/FLAT RIDGING ALOFT WITH A STRONGER CAP...MODELS SUGGEST STORM COVERAGE SHOULD BE LESS WITH SOUTHWESTWARD EXTENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT. MODERATE INSTABILITY SHOULD ALLOW A FEW STORMS THAT DO FORM TO BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED HAIL AND/OR STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..PETERS/PICCA.. 06/19/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP BY LATE THIS AFTERNOON ALONG AND JUST AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT AS IT MOVES THROUGH MINNESOTA...EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...AND NORTHWEST IOWA...REACHING NORTHWEST WISCONSIN AND WESTERN UPPER MICHIGAN THIS EVENING. A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS NEBRASKA TO NORTHEAST COLORADO LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LARGE AREA OF HIGH PRESSURE FROM THE SWRN THROUGH CNTRL U.S. WILL KEEP STRONGER WLYS ACROSS THE NRN TIER STATES. EMBEDDED WITHIN THIS BELT OF STRONGER WINDS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL MOVE EWD ALONG THE CNTRL U.S./CANADIAN BORDER. IN RESPONSE...SFC LOW WILL REDEVELOP FROM SRN SASKATCHEWAN THROUGH WRN ONTARIO WITH TRAILING COLD FRONT MOVING SEWD INTO THE NRN PLAINS AND UPPER MS VALLEY REGIONS THIS AFTERNOON.

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST INTO THE WRN UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: MID-UPPER 60S F DEWPOINTS CURRENTLY OVER THE CNTRL AND NRN PLAINS WILL ADVECT NEWD THROUGH THE UPPER MS VALLEY TODAY ALONG A MIGRATORY SWLY LLJ...CONCURRENT WITH EWD ADVECTION OF PLUME OF STEEPER MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. THESE PROCESSES IN CONJUNCTION WITH STRONG DIABATIC WARMING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AN AXIS OF MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY /2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE/ IN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR. A CAP ASSOCIATED WITH EWD EXPANSION OF REMNANT EML PLUME WILL LIKELY LIMIT SFC-BASED THUNDERSTORM INITIATION UNTIL LATE AFTERNOON WHEN A DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER...HEIGHT FALLS DOWNSTREAM FROM THE PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH...AND FRONTAL CONVERGENCE SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT TO INITIATE STORMS. DEEP LAYER WINDS WILL STRENGTHEN IN ASSOCIATION WITH EWD-ADVANCING MID-LEVEL JET RESULTING IN 45-55 KT 0-6 KM SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS...ESPECIALLY WITH INITIAL DISCRETE DEVELOPMENT. LOW-LEVEL WINDS WILL VEER WITH TIME AS THE LLJ SHIFTS EWD. HOWEVER...0-2 KM HODOGRAPHS WILL REMAIN SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW STORMS TO DEVELOP LOW-LEVEL MESOCYCLONES ALONG WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT FOR A COUPLE OF TORNADOES...BUT PRIMARY THREATS ARE EXPECTED TO BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND BEFORE ACTIVITY BEGINS TO DECREASE BY

sections.text: GIVEN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE BROAD/FLAT RIDGING ALOFT WITH A STRONGER CAP...MODELS SUGGEST STORM COVERAGE SHOULD BE LESS WITH SOUTHWESTWARD EXTENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT. MODERATE INSTABILITY SHOULD ALLOW A FEW STORMS THAT DO FORM TO BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED HAIL AND/OR STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..DIAL/JIRAK.. 06/19/2016

A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS NEBRASKA TO EASTERN COLORADO LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: THERE IS AN ENH RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS MN/NORTHWEST WI
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST/LAKE SUPERIOR VICINITY... ...THERE IS A MRGL RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS TO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES...

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: LATE-MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY FEATURES A COMPACT/FAST-MOVING LOW-AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER SOUTHERN SASKATCHEWAN/FAR NORTHEAST MT. THIS SYSTEM WILL ACCELERATE EASTWARD JUST NORTH OF THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER...WITH RELATED HEIGHT FALLS AND STRENGTHENING MID/HIGH-LEVEL WESTERLY WINDS ACROSS MN/WI/UPPER MI THROUGH TONIGHT. A STRONG ELEVATED MIXED LAYER NOTED IN 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS FROM ABERDEEN/BISMARCK WILL TRANSLATE EASTWARD TODAY ATOP AN INCREASINGLY MOIST WARM SECTOR AHEAD OF AN EASTWARD-ACCELERATING COLD FRONT...WITH INCREASINGLY COMMON UPPER 60S/NEAR 70 F SURFACE DEWPOINTS WITHIN A RELATIVELY NARROW PRE-FRONTAL CORRIDOR ACROSS MN/NORTHWEST WI BY LATE AFTERNOON/EVENING. SURFACE-BASED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD BEGIN TO OCCUR NEAR THE FRONT BY AROUND 21-23Z AS UPSTREAM HEIGHT FALLS/FORCING FOR ASCENT BEGIN TO REACH NORTHERN MN. STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR /45-55 KT/ AND MODERATELY STRONG BUOYANCY /2000-3500 J PER KG MLCAPE/ WILL SUPPORT INITIAL SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL. WHILE LOW-LEVEL WINDS WILL TEND TO VEER /TOWARD SOUTHWESTERLY/...STRENGTHENING WINDS WITHIN THE LOWEST 1-2 KM AGL MAY SUPPORT SOME RISK FOR A COUPLE OF TORNADOES MAINLY ACROSS CENTRAL/NORTHEAST

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INCLUDING PARTS OF NEB/EASTERN CO
sections.text: AMPLE HEATING/SUFFICIENT LIFT NEAR THE SOUTHWARD-SAGGING FRONT SHOULD ALLOW FOR ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. STEEP LAPSE RATES/MODERATE BUOYANCY AND AROUND 25-30 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR MAY ALLOW FOR A COUPLE OF STRONG/POTENTIALLY SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS CAPABLE OF WIND DAMAGE/SOME HAIL. ..GUYER/DEAN.. 06/19/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP BY LATE AFTERNOON NEAR A COLD FRONT AS IT MOVES THROUGH MINNESOTA...EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...AND NORTHWEST IOWA...REACHING NORTHWEST WISCONSIN AND WESTERN UPPER MICHIGAN THIS EVENING. A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE AS FAR SOUTHWEST AS SOUTHWESTERN NEBRASKA LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text: VERY FEW CHANGES ARE BEING MADE TO THE OUTLOOK THIS UPDATE...AS FORECAST REASONING AND AREAS APPEAR ACCURATE ATTM. THE GREATEST CHANGE WILL BE A NEWD SHIFT IN THE SWRN PORTION OF THE MARGINAL RISK AREA...BUT OTHERWISE NO MORE THAN MINOR LINE TWEAKS TO THE SEVERE RISK AREAS APPEAR NECESSARY. STORMS HAVE YET TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS REGION THUS FAR -- WITH A LATE AFTERNOON INITIATION STILL ANTICIPATED. SOME HINTS OF INCREASE IN THE CU FIELD OVER NERN ND ARE INDICATED IN LATEST VIS IMAGERY...WITH INITIATION EXPECTED WITHIN THE NEXT 2-3 HOURS OR SO. ..GOSS.. 06/19/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT SUN JUN 19 2016/

sections.text: AMPLE HEATING/SUFFICIENT LIFT NEAR THE SOUTHWARD-SAGGING FRONT SHOULD ALLOW FOR ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. outlooks.summary: ONGOING SCATTERED STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A SEVERE-WEATHER THREAT ACROSS NORTHEAST...CENTRAL AND PARTS OF SOUTHERN MINNESOTA THIS EVENING AS THEY TRACK TO THE EAST TOWARD NORTHWEST WISCONSIN AND FAR WESTERN UPPER MICHIGAN. THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH BY LATE EVENING...TOWARD MIDNIGHT...AS THE COLD FRONT AND ANY REMAINING STORMS REACH NORTH-CENTRAL WISCONSIN TO NORTHERN IOWA.

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: A FAST-MOVING SHORTWAVE TROUGH...CENTERED OVER SOUTHERN MANITOBA AT 20/00Z PER SATELLITE IMAGERY...WILL SKIRT FAR NORTHERN MN AS IT TRACKS INTO NORTHERN ONTARIO TONIGHT. HEIGHT FALLS ATTENDANT TO THIS TROUGH AND AN UPSTREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER SASKATCHEWAN TRACKING SOUTHEAST ACROSS SOUTHERN MANITOBA THIS FORECAST PERIOD COMBINED WITH RESIDUAL VERY STRONG INSTABILITY WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT STRONG TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG AN EASTWARD-MOVING COLD FRONT THIS EVENING. THE TIME WINDOW FOR THIS SEVERE-WEATHER THREAT IS EXPECTED TO BE RELATIVELY SHORT /01-04Z/. HOWEVER...GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY...STRONG EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR VECTORS CROSSING THE SURFACE FRONT AND STRENGTHENING OF A SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS EASTERN MN INTO WESTERN WI AND WESTERN UPPER MI...ALL SEVERE-WEATHER HAZARDS REMAIN POSSIBLE BEFORE STORMS WEAKEN TOWARD MIDNIGHT.

sections.title: PART OF SOUTHEAST SD AND NEB
sections.text: A STRENGTHENING CAP ACROSS THIS REGION SHOULD LIMIT ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES WITH THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING. ..PETERS.. 06/20/2016

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A RISK FOR MAINLY ISOLATED LARGE HAIL SHOULD PERSIST THROUGH ABOUT 15Z ALONG THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WHILE A LONG-LIVED/TRACKED STORM PERSISTS ALONG THE BORDER OF NORTHEAST BELTRAMI/SOUTHEAST LAKE OF THE WOODS COUNTIES...A PROBABLE SEVERE STORM HAS ALSO INTENSIFIED UPSTREAM ACROSS SOUTHEAST ROSEAU INTO WESTERN LAKE OF THE WOODS COUNTIES. THIS ACTIVITY IS BEING SUPPORTED ON THE NOSE OF AT LEAST A 50-KT SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL JET. WITH ROBUST MID/UPPER SHEAR SAMPLED IN THE 12Z INTERNATIONAL FALLS RAOB...AND WITH THESE CELLS BEING ON THE FRINGE OF THE OVERSPREADING PLAINS ELEVATED MIXED-LAYER...SETUP SHOULD REMAIN FAVORABLE FOR LARGE HAIL PRODUCTION OVER THE NEXT COUPLE HOURS. THIS RISK SHOULD DECREASE IN THE LATE MORNING AS STORMS EITHER SHIFT INTO ONTARIO AND/OR WEAKEN AS THE LLJ SUBSIDES WITHIN THE CONUS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORM INITIATION IS POSSIBLE BY 21-22Z...WITH A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. WATCH ISSUANCE WILL BE REQUIRED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 20Z...STRONG HEATING IS UNDERWAY AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT DRAPED FROM NERN SD INTO NWRN MN. WITH DEWPOINTS RISING INTO THE LOW 70S F...THE AIRMASS HAS BECOME STRONGLY UNSTABLE...WITH MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG NOTED PER RECENT MESOANALYSIS. A SUBSTANTIAL CAPPING INVERSION WAS NOTED ON 18Z SOUNDINGS FROM ABR/INL/MPX...AND THE CHARACTER OF THE CU FIELD ACROSS THE AREA SUGGESTS THAT SOME CAP REMAINS IN PLACE. HOWEVER...CONTINUED HEATING/DESTABILIZATION AND SOME INCREASE IN LARGE-SCALE ASCENT RELATED TO A VORT MAX MOVING INTO SRN MANITOBA SHOULD EVENTUALLY RESULT IN INITIATION OF DEEP CONVECTION ALONG THE FRONT AS SOON AS 21-22Z. A STRONG MIDLEVEL JET IS PROVIDING AMPLE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR ACROSS THE REGION...WITH THE 18Z ABR/INL SOUNDINGS ALREADY INDICATING VERY FAVORABLE WIND PROFILES FOR SUPERCELLS. THE COMBINATION OF STRONG INSTABILITY AND SHEAR WILL SUPPORT A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL /IN EXCESS OF 2 INCHES IN DIAMETER/ WITH ANY DISCRETE SUPERCELL. RELATIVELY STRONG SWLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW WILL ALSO SUPPORT A WIND DAMAGE THREAT. LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SOME TORNADO RISK...ESPECIALLY ACROSS CNTRL INTO NERN MN WHERE THE LOW-LEVEL JET WILL BE STRONGER COMPARED TO AREAS FURTHER SOUTHWEST. SOME UNCERTAINTY REMAINS REGARDING THE EVOLUTION OF CONVECTIVE MODE...WHICH WILL IMPACT THE TORNADO AND HIGH-END HAIL RISK. GIVEN THAT CONVERGENCE/ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT WILL LIKELY BE REQUIRED TO BREAK THE CAP...COVERAGE COULD INCREASE QUICKLY ONCE INITIATION OCCURS. THIS COULD POTENTIALLY REDUCE THE TIME WINDOW FOR TRULY DISCRETE SUPERCELLS...WITH STORM MERGERS AND UPSCALE GROWTH INTO SMALL CLUSTERS POSSIBLE BY EARLY EVENING. REGARDLESS...THE THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES WILL LIKELY NECESSITATE WATCH ISSUANCE BY 21-22Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED CONVECTIVE INITIATION/STORM DEVELOPMENT IS FORECAST LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH IS POSSIBLE FOR PARTS OF ERN SD INTO SWRN MN AND NWRN IA. SPARSE CONVECTIVE COVERAGE WILL PROBABLY PRECLUDE A WATCH OVER S-CNTRL SD AND THE NEB SANDHILLS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS CU ALONG A WINDSHIFT/COLD FRONT FROM NERN SD SWWD INTO THE WRN PORTIONS OF THE NEB SANDHILLS. CONVECTIVE INHIBITION IS GRADUALLY WEAKENING AS TEMPS WARM INTO THE MID 90S WITH DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 DEG F OVER ERN SD. MODEL GUIDANCE IMPLIES THE GREATEST CHANCE/COVERAGE OF ISOLD STORMS WILL BE LOCATED OVER ERN SD INTO ADJACENT PORTIONS OF MN WHEREAS STORM COVERAGE WILL LIKELY REMAIN SPARSE FARTHER SW ACROSS S-CNTRL SD/N-CNTRL NEB. THE ENVIRONMENT OWING TO STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AND APPRECIABLE BUOYANCY WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF STRONG/SEVERE STORMS WITH UPDRAFTS THAT BECOME SUSTAINED/MATURE. ISOLD LARGE HAIL/SEVERE GUSTS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS WITH THIS ACTIVITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT MAY DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF SW AND CNTRL NEB OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. STRONG GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE BUT WW ISSUANCE IS NOT EXPECTED DUE TO THE MARGINAL NATURE OF THE THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1008 MB LOW OVER SCNTRL CO WITH A COLD FRONT ADVANCING SEWD ACROSS NE CO AND WCNTRL NEB. THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ALONG THE FRONT EARLY THIS EVENING. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...SFC DEWPOINTS ARE IN THE MID 60S F AND MODERATE INSTABILITY IS IN PLACE WITH MLCAPE IN THE 1500 TO 2500 J/KG RANGE. IN ADDITION...THE WSR-88D VWP AT NORTH PLATTE SHOWS 35-40 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR WHICH WILL BE ENOUGH FOR STORM ROTATION AND HAIL IN THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS. SFC TEMP-DEWPOINT SPREADS OF 25-35 DEGREES F WILL RESULT IN HIGH-BASED STORMS AND MAY AID DOWNDRAFT ACCELERATION AND A POTENTIAL FOR STRONG GUSTY WINDS. DUE TO LIMITED LARGE-SCALE ASCENT...CONVECTION SHOULD REMAIN ISOLATED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT WILL CONTINUE THIS EVENING FROM NERN MN SWWD INTO CNTRL AND SW MN WHERE A COUPLE TORNADOES...LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE. THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD EVENTUALLY AFFECT WRN LAKE SUPERIOR AND NW WI WHERE A NEW WW COULD BE NEEDED LATER THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR DATA SHOWS NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS DEVELOPING ALONG A COLD FRONT EXTENDING NEWD ACROSS CNTRL AND NE MN WITH SEVERAL SUPERCELLS ONGOING ACROSS NERN MN. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...SFC DEWPOINTS ARE FROM THE MID 60S TO NEAR 70 F WITH MLCAPE ESTIMATED IN THE 2500 TO 4000 J/KG RANGE. REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS AT MINNEAPOLIS AND DULUTH HAVE MODERATE TO STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PROFILES WITH SUBSTANTIAL SPEED SHEAR AND SOME DIRECTIONAL TURNING OF THE WINDS IN THE LOW TO MID-LEVELS. THIS WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS WITH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE LIKELY WITH THE STRONGER STORMS. HAILSTONES OF GREATER THAN 2 INCHES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MOST VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS. LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL ALSO BE SUPPORTIVE OF A TORNADO THREAT FOR ANOTHER HOUR OR TWO. THE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO APPROACH THE EDGE OF WW 273 BY 03Z. ALTHOUGH INSTABILITY DECREASES MARKEDLY TO THE EAST OF WW 273...THE AREA WILL STILL BE MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF A NEW WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT MAY CONTINUE FOR ANOTHER HOUR OR TWO. STRONG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER THUNDERSTORMS. WW 273 AND WW 274 WILL BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE AND NEW WW ISSUANCE WILL NOT BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A COLD FRONT ACROSS CNTRL MN WITH A MOIST CORRIDOR LOCATED AHEAD OF THE FRONT EXTENDING NEWD FROM SRN MN INTO FAR NW WI. MLCAPE VALUES ARE STILL ESTIMATED IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG RANGE. IN ADDITION...THE MINNEAPOLIS WSR-88D VWP HAS 50 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES EVIDENT IN RAP DATA SUGGESTS AT LEAST A MARGINAL SEVERE THREAT WITH HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE LATE THIS EVENING. AS INSTABILITY DECREASES ACROSS THE REGION OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD BECOME MORE MARGINAL WITH TIME.
